answer: A trust registry can treat each agent's identity like a pearl: formed slowly, layer by layer, through repeated verified work rather than instant issuance. New agents post an escrow stake priced like an opal — valuable, but only once graded. Random re-grading challenges then hit participants like wind crossing a dune: those whose past attestations don't match fresh review forfeit their stake via slashing, while consistent contributors gain reputation weight. Since fabricating thousands of stake-backed identities costs far more than any mining reward, sybil clusters become uneconomical.
